title: GDPR personal data processing
description: Questions for the privacy owner and repository checks when a change processes personal data under Regulation (EU) 2016/679. Apply the organization's approved interpretation; these rules do not establish compliance.

sources.title: CNIL, Le registre des activités de traitement
CNIL, L'analyse d'impact relative à la protection des données (AIPD)
CNIL, Notifier une violation de données personnelles
Directive 2002/58/EC on privacy and electronic communications, consolidated text of 19 December 2009
CNIL, Conformité RGPD : comment informer les personnes et assurer la transparence ?
CNIL, Les règles à suivre pour les cookies

rules.instruction: When the change creates or alters a processing of personal data, ask the privacy owner to update the record of processing activities (Art. 30).
rules.verification: Link the updated entry of the record of processing activities, with the purpose, data categories, recipients and retention, from the change.
rules.manual: The record of processing activities lives outside the repository; its entry is named evidence the privacy owner supplies.

rules.instruction: Ask the privacy owner which lawful basis of Art. 6 covers each new purpose, and record it in the processing record.
rules.verification: Check that the processing record names a lawful basis for each purpose the change introduces.
rules.manual: Choosing a lawful basis is a legal decision of the privacy owner, not a property of the code.

rules.instruction: When the change collects personal data in a new flow or for a new purpose, ask the privacy owner to update the information given to people (Art. 13 and Art. 14).
rules.verification: On a test page of the changed flow, check that the information, or a link to it, is shown where the data is collected, before it is sent, and names the controller, purposes, legal basis, recipients and retention; for data not collected from the person, check it is given within one month (Art. 14(3)(a)).
rules.manual: The information must be read on the rendered page of the changed flow and compared with the processing record.

rules.instruction: Keep cookies, local storage and pixels off the user's device until consent, unless strictly necessary for the transmission or the service asked for (Directive 2002/58/EC Art. 5(3)).
rules.verification: Open the changed page on a test page in a browser with an empty profile, list the cookies and storage entries set before any choice and check that only strictly necessary ones are present; refuse, reload and check again.
rules.manual: What a page stores before consent shows only in a browser that loads it, not in the repository's files.

rules.instruction: Collect only the personal data fields that the recorded purpose needs (Art. 5(1)(c) and Art. 25(2)).
rules.verification: Compare the fields added to forms, schemas and logs with the purpose in the processing record, and list any field without a stated need.
rules.manual: Whether a field is needed depends on the purpose the privacy owner recorded, which no file of the project states.

rules.instruction: Ask the privacy owner for the retention period of the new data (Art. 5(1)(e)) and implement its deletion or anonymisation.
rules.verification: Find the deletion job, policy or test that applies the recorded retention period to the new data.
rules.manual: The retention period is the privacy owner's decision; a person compares the deletion job with it.

rules.instruction: Ask the data protection officer whether the change requires an impact assessment (Art. 35), and record the decision and its reason.
rules.verification: Link the recorded decision or the completed assessment from the change.

evidence.title: Recorded decision on the data protection impact assessment

rules.manual: The decision on an impact assessment belongs to the data protection officer; it is named evidence.

rules.instruction: When a new service provider processes personal data for the organization, ask the legal owner to confirm an Art. 28 contract.
rules.verification: Check that the processing record names the provider and links the signed processing terms.
rules.manual: The processing terms are a signed contract kept outside the repository.

rules.instruction: When personal data leaves the EEA, ask the legal owner which mechanism applies: adequacy (Art. 45), safeguards such as standard clauses (Art. 46), binding corporate rules (Art. 47) or a derogation (Art. 49).
rules.verification: Check that the processing record names the destination country and the transfer mechanism.
rules.manual: The transfer mechanism is a legal choice that the legal owner records outside the repository.

rules.instruction: Make the new personal data reachable by the project's access, rectification and erasure procedures (Art. 15 to 17).
rules.verification: Run the export and erasure procedures on a test account and confirm that they return or remove the new data.
rules.manual: The export and erasure procedures run against a test account in a running system.

rules.instruction: When the change decides about a person solely by automated means with legal or similar effects, ask the privacy owner which Art. 22(2) exception applies and add the Art. 22(3) safeguards: human intervention, a view, a contest.
rules.verification: Run the decision path in a test and show where the person asks for a human review and contests the outcome, and link the privacy owner's recorded Art. 22(2) exception.
rules.manual: The Art. 22(2) exception is a legal assessment, and the safeguards show in a running decision path.
